title: The tools of good works (ch. 4)
hookLine: a list including keep death daily before your eyes and never despair of God's mercy

lines: GRAB THE ONE THE JOB NEEDS.
cards: A pegboard on a garage wall. Each tool hangs on its own hook, with its outline drawn around it in marker, so you can see at a glance what's missing. Hammer.
Level. The good screwdriver somebody borrowed. Nobody uses every tool every day; you grab the one the job needs.
Chapter four of Saint Benedict's Rule is a pegboard like that, for the inner life. A long list, hung up in plain sight.

teach.b: Benedict doesn't explain the tools. He just lists them, one short line after another.

The first is the great commandment, as Jesus gives it in the Douay-Rheims: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole mind." Then, love your neighbor as yourself.
After that the list runs on, some from the Ten Commandments, some from the Sermon on the Mount, some Benedict's own. Prefer nothing to the love of Christ. Don't give a false peace.
Make peace with someone you've quarreled with before the sun goes down. Pray for your enemies. Then two that stop people.
Keep death daily before your eyes. That sounds grim, but in the Rule it's meant to focus, not to frighten: if today could be the last, what actually matters?
And at the very end, the tool Benedict saves for last: never despair of God's mercy. Why last? A monk who tries the others will fail at some of them, maybe most, on a bad day.
The list seems to expect that. The final tool is for when the rest have slipped out of your hands.

teach.h: THE WORKSHOP IS WHERE YOU ARE.
teach.b: Then Benedict names the workshop: the enclosure of the monastery, and staying put in the community.
Not somewhere far off. Right where you already are. And if despair ever feels heavy or dangerous, you don't have to carry it alone: call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

how: Benedictines read chapter 4 of the Rule in turn with the other chapters, and some readers use the list as an examination of conscience.

games.q: what does “the tools of good works” mean?
o: Benedict's list of short rules for the inner life
the farm tools each monk was handed for work
the chores given out to every monk each morning

games.q: the tools of good works — tap the pairs.
p: love God with your whole heart

s: Benedict explains each tool at length
he just lists them, one short line after another.
the list ends with never despair of God's mercy
the last tool, for when the others have slipped.
for Benedict, the workshop is somewhere far away
it's the monastery and staying put in the community: right where you are.

games.q: you're Benedict, finishing your long list of tools. which one do you put last?
o: love God with your whole heart.
keep death daily before your eyes.
games.why: never despair of God's mercy. a monk will fail at some of the others; this is the tool for when they slip.

practice: Let a few of today's tools pass slowly through your mind: love your neighbor as yourself, make peace before the sun goes down, pray for your enemies, keep death before your eyes, never despair of God's mercy.
Notice which one your day actually needs, not the most impressive one but the one that fits the job, and hold it for a while. If you pray, ask God for help using it well.

wordCard.voice: The tools of good works. Chapter four of Benedict's Rule: a long list of short instructions for the inner life, ending with never despair of God's mercy. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin, the last line of the Rule's list: never to despair of God's mercy.

carryVoice: Your line: never despair. When the other tools slip, the last one is still hanging on the board. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole mind.
